best-broadway-plays.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays: March 2026

As Broadway enters the spring season of 2026, the theatrical landscape offers an eclectic mix of original works and franchise adaptations. This month's selection of four plays averages a solid 77 out of 100 from critics, reflecting a range of both innovative storytelling and spectacle-driven productions.

Leading the pack is **Oh, Mary!**, Cole Escola's absurdist comedy that reimagines Mary Todd Lincoln as a cabaret-obsessed narcissist with a drinking problem. With a score of 84 out of 100 across 33 reviews, the farce has emerged as the critical favorite, earning praise for its audacious premise and riotous execution. The show represents a boldly irreverent take on historical drama that continues to resonate with audiences and critics alike.

Close behind is **Harry Potter and the Cursed Child**, which maintains its position as a technical marvel. Scoring 82 out of 100 from 69 reviews, the production remains a masterclass in stagecraft and magical illusions, even as critics note unevenness in its narrative structure. The sheer theatrical wizardry on display continues to justify its status as one of Broadway's most visually stunning experiences.

At the other end of the spectrum, **Stranger Things: The First Shadow** demonstrates the challenges of adapting popular screen franchises for the stage. Despite impressive special effects and technical ambition, the three-hour prequel receives mixed notices, with critics finding the narrative overstuffed despite its visual accomplishments.

Whether you're drawn to sharp-witted satire, magical spectacle, or immersive world-building, this month's offerings provide multiple entry points into Broadway's diverse theatrical landscape.

# Best Broadway Shows from 2020

As we look back in March 2026 at the Broadway productions that opened in 2020, we're reminded of a season that was dramatically cut short by the COVID-19 pandemic, leaving many of these shows with truncated runs and uncertain futures. The five productions that made the strongest critical impact before the shutdown represent a diverse snapshot of theatrical ambition—from bold reimaginings of classics to long-awaited debuts of important American dramas.

Leading the pack is a grittier reboot of **Les Misérables** at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre, earning an 83/100 from critics who largely embraced its fresh approach to the beloved musical, though the production has its detractors. Close behind is **A Soldier's Play**, Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama that finally received its overdue Broadway premiere in a stellar revival, proving the work's examination of race and justice in the military remains urgently relevant with a 78/100 score across 29 reviews.

The season's more divisive offerings include Laura Linney's solo turn in **My Name is Lucy Barton**, an adaptation that splits critics despite universal acclaim for Linney's performance, and Ivo van Hove's radical **West Side Story** reimagining, which generates passionate responses on both sides. Rounding out the selection is **Grand Horizons**, a well-acted if familiar comedy elevated by Broadway veterans Jane Alexander and James Cromwell.

With an average critical score of 74/100 across these five productions, the class of 2020 represents a season of artistic ambition interrupted, offering contemporary audiences a fascinating glimpse at what might have been. Explore our detailed reviews to discover which of these productions might still resonate with your theatrical tastes.

best-broadway-shows-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows from 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the shows that debuted in 2021 remain some of Broadway's most critically acclaimed productions. That year marked a pivotal moment for theater: Broadway's reopening after the pandemic shutdown brought an extraordinary wave of creativity, with productions ranging from intimate experimental works to spectacular revivals that redefined classics for new audiences.

Leading the pack is **Dana H.**, Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama that continues to mesmerize audiences with Deirdre O'Connell's stunning lip-sync performance. This challenging work pushes theatrical boundaries in ways few Broadway productions dare attempt. Close behind, **The Phantom of the Opera** and **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club** demonstrate the enduring power of musical theater—the former through Andrew Lloyd Webber's timeless spectacle, the latter through Rebecca Frecknall's immersive reimagining that transforms the entire Playhouse Theatre into the Kit Kat Club.

The 2021 season also showcased exceptional solo performances, with **Lackawanna Blues** featuring Ruben Santiago-Hudson's virtuosic portrayal of dozens of characters, while **The Lehman Trilogy** offered an epic ensemble piece tracing 150 years of American capitalism. Experimental works like **Is This a Room**, built entirely from FBI transcripts, proved that documentary theater could deliver pulse-pounding drama.

The year's musicals brought both innovation and joy: Marianne Elliott's gender-swapped **Company** revitalized Sondheim's masterwork, **Pass Over** marked Broadway's powerful reopening statement, and **SIX** transformed Tudor history into an exuberant pop concert.

With an impressive average critic score of 81/100 across these ten productions, 2021's Broadway season set a high bar for theatrical excellence. Whether you're drawn to experimental docudrama, reimagined classics, or innovative musicals, these shows represent some of the finest work Broadway has to offer.

These productions, which debuted in the brief window before the pandemic shutdown, continue to resonate with audiences and critics alike.

Among the five notable plays from this period, **Les Misérables** stands out with the highest critical score (83/100), earning praise for its grittier approach at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre. This reimagined production demonstrates how classic material can find new life through bold reinterpretation, though the rebooted vision doesn't win over every traditionalist.

**A Soldier's Play** marks a significant cultural moment, bringing Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama to Broadway for the first time. With 29 reviews and a strong 78/100 score, this stellar revival proves the enduring relevance of its examination of race, power, and justice within the military—themes that remain urgently contemporary six years later.

The remaining productions showcase Broadway's range: Laura Linney's solo turn in **My Name is Lucy Barton** divides critics despite her luminous performance, while **Grand Horizons** offers familiar but well-executed boulevard comedy elevated by veteran performers. Ivo van Hove's radical **West Side Story** reimagining proves the most divisive, with its bold visual approach and fresh interpretation earning both passionate admirers and skeptics.

With an average critical score of 74/100 across these five productions, the 2020 season—brief though it was—delivered thoughtful, ambitious work that continues to inform conversations about what Broadway can be. Explore the detailed reviews to discover which of these productions aligns with your theatrical tastes.

# Best Broadway Plays of 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway shows that opened in 2021 represent a remarkable moment of theatrical rebirth. Following the pandemic shutdown, these productions didn't just reopen theaters—they redefined what Broadway could be.

The year's most critically acclaimed offering is **Dana H.**, an unconventional docudrama that continues to mesmerize audiences with Deirdre O'Connell's stunning lip-sync performance to real interview recordings. This experimental work proves that Broadway remains a home for daring theatrical innovation. Meanwhile, **The Lehman Trilogy** stands as an epic achievement, with critics praising its extraordinary performances and stunning direction as it traces 164 years of American capitalism through one family's rise and fall.

The season also showcases remarkable range, from **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club**'s immersive reimagining that transforms the entire Playhouse Theatre into pre-war Berlin, to intimate verbatim pieces like **Is This a Room**, which turns an FBI transcript into gripping drama. Gender-swapped revivals like **Company** breathe new life into classic material, while new works such as **Pass Over** and **Clyde's** tackle urgent contemporary themes. Even long-running spectacles like **The Phantom of the Opera** and pop-infused newcomers like **SIX** find their place in this diverse landscape.

With an impressive average critic score of 81/100 across these ten productions, the 2021 season demonstrates Broadway's resilience and artistic vitality during a pivotal moment. Whether you're drawn to experimental docudrama, epic storytelling, or reimagined classics, these productions offer essential theatrical experiences worth discovering before they close.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays from 2022

As we look back from March 2026, the 2022 Broadway season stands as a remarkable year of theatrical achievement, distinguished by its celebration of Pulitzer Prize-winning works and bold new voices. With an impressive average critic score of 83/100 across our featured productions, this collection represents some of the most acclaimed theater to grace Broadway stages in recent memory.

Leading the pack is **Kimberly Akimbo**, the quirky musical about a teenage girl with a rare aging condition that critics have embraced as a near-perfect gem, masterfully balancing comedy and heartbreak. Close behind, **Into the Woods** offers a stripped-down Sondheim revival that serves as both a triumphant tribute to the late composer and a showcase for stellar performances. **A Strange Loop**, Michael R. Jackson's meta-musical about a Black gay artist struggling to write a musical about a Black gay artist, rounds out the top tier with its brazenly original approach to storytelling.

The year proved particularly significant for Pulitzer Prize winners, with five productions—A Strange Loop, Topdog/Underdog, Leopoldstadt, Between Riverside and Crazy, How I Learned to Drive, and Cost of Living—demonstrating the enduring power of award-recognized drama. From Suzan-Lori Parks' electrifying exploration of brotherhood and betrayal to Paula Vogel's unflinching examination of abuse, these works tackle complex themes with intelligence and emotional depth.

Whether you're discovering these productions for the first time or revisiting favorites, this collection offers a comprehensive look at a season that balanced entertainment with artistic ambition, proving Broadway's continued vitality as a home for both crowd-pleasing spectacle and challenging drama.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2023

As of March 2026, the exceptional class of plays that opened on Broadway in 2023 continues to resonate with audiences and critics alike, representing one of the strongest theatrical years in recent memory. With an impressive average critic score of 82/100 across our featured productions, these ten shows demonstrate the remarkable range and vitality of contemporary American theater.

Leading the field is Maria Friedman's triumphant revival of **Merrily We Roll Along**, which has definitively redeemed Stephen Sondheim's notorious 1981 flop through emotionally resonant performances and fresh directorial vision. Close behind, **Stranger Things: The First Shadow** proves that theatrical adaptations of popular media can transcend mere fan service, earning acclaim for its technical wizardry and compelling storytelling that stands independent of its source material.

The year's offerings span an impressive spectrum: from Branden Jacobs-Jenkins's searing family drama **Appropriate**, featuring powerhouse performances led by Sarah Paulson, to the long-overdue revival of Ossie Davis's **Purlie Victorious**, which demonstrates how classic satire can speak urgently to contemporary audiences. Musical theater also shines with Ben Platt and Micaela Diamond's acclaimed performances in the timely **Parade** revival, while intimate solo work finds representation in Alex Edelman's brilliant **Just for Us**.

Rounding out this distinguished list are ambitious productions like **Sweeney Todd**, the Pulitzer Prize-winning **Fat Ham**, the immersive rock drama **Stereophonic**, and the rhythmically infectious **Buena Vista Social Club**—each offering distinct theatrical experiences that have enriched Broadway's cultural landscape.

Whether you're seeking classic revivals reimagined for modern audiences or bold new voices pushing theatrical boundaries, the plays of 2023 offer compelling reasons to experience live theater at its finest.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in 2024

As March 2026 arrives, the Broadway shows that premiered in 2024 continue to demonstrate remarkable staying power and critical acclaim. This period has proven to be one of the most diverse and creatively ambitious seasons in recent memory, with productions ranging from intimate character studies to large-scale musical spectacles earning recognition from critics and audiences alike.

Leading the field is **Stereophonic**, David Adjmi's meticulously crafted drama about a 1970s rock band, which critics have embraced as a theatrical marvel for its authentic portrayal of the creative process. The production's immersive approach to depicting the tensions and triumphs of making music has resonated deeply with reviewers, earning it the highest critical score among 2024's openings.

Also standing out is **Operation Mincemeat**, a grassroots sensation that successfully made the leap from smaller venues to Broadway. Critics praise its inventive energy and ensemble work, proving that unconventional productions can find mainstream success. Meanwhile, **Maybe Happy Ending** has charmed reviewers as one of Broadway's most original musicals in years, with its robot love story offering both emotional depth and creative risk-taking.

The ten productions featured here represent a strong average critic score of 83/100, reflecting a season that balanced artistic ambition with accessibility. From Cole Escola's irreverent **Oh, Mary!** to classic revivals like **Gypsy** and **Oliver!**, the 2024 season offered something for every theatrical taste, whether audiences sought bold new voices or fresh interpretations of beloved works.

For theatergoers planning their Broadway visits, these critically acclaimed productions offer proven quality across multiple genres and styles.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays

As spring 2026 arrives, Broadway continues to showcase the exceptional plays that defined the 2025 season, offering audiences a diverse array of theatrical experiences from intimate dramas to spectacular family entertainment.

The season's strongest offerings demonstrate the enduring power of both classic American drama and contemporary voices. Ivo van Hove's minimalist revival of **All My Sons** leads the field, earning widespread acclaim for its emotional intensity and exceptional ensemble work that strips Arthur Miller's tragedy to its raw essentials. Close behind, the 20th-anniversary revival of **The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee** proves the musical's timeless appeal, with critics celebrating its joyous spirit and airtight construction. Meanwhile, **Paddington The Musical** has charmed audiences and critics alike, with its remarkably lifelike bear puppet earning recognition as a genuine theatrical marvel.

The season also highlights important contemporary playwrights, with Sanaz Toossi's Pulitzer-winning **English** offering a smart, sensitive exploration of language and identity, while Branden Jacobs-Jenkins delivers another characteristically sharp family drama with **Purpose**. Classic musicals receive fresh relevance through revivals like **Ragtime**, which resonates with particular timeliness and features Joshua Henry's powerhouse performance, and more unconventional offerings like **Dead Outlaw**, a darkly comic musical chronicling outlaw Elmer McCurdy's bizarre posthumous journey.

With an impressive average critic score of 84/100 across these ten productions, the 2025 season demonstrates Broadway's continued vitality in presenting both carefully reconsidered classics and bold new voices. Whether you're drawn to austere dramatic intensity, heartwarming family entertainment, or provocative contemporary storytelling, these productions offer compelling reasons to experience live theater this spring.

**Every Brilliant Thing** stands as the sole representative of 2026's new play openings, earning a solid 76/100 from critics. The production brings its intimate exploration of depression, resilience, and the small joys that make life worth living to Broadway audiences, offering theatergoers a deeply personal and participatory theatrical experience that has resonated with audiences in smaller venues worldwide.

With an average critic score of 76/100 across this limited opening slate, the year's dramatic offerings have started on respectable footing, though the season clearly awaits additional productions to provide a fuller picture of Broadway's creative direction. The sparse calendar reflects broader industry patterns, as producers continue to navigate economic considerations and strategic timing for new work.

The theatrical landscape typically expands considerably as spring progresses into the traditionally robust fall season, when producers unveil their most ambitious projects. This measured start to 2026 suggests that major announcements and openings likely await in the coming months, as theaters finalize their programming and casting for what may prove to be a more active second half of the year.

For theatergoers planning their Broadway visits in the weeks ahead, the current selection offers quality over quantity, with opportunities to experience intimate storytelling in ways that larger productions cannot replicate.
